== Biography ==
William Glasgow was recorded as the 40-year-old head of house 1 at Cloughgaldenagh, Dunaghy, County Antrim, in the census of '''30 March 1851'''. He was a weaver, could read and write, and was living with his wife [[Unknown-540868|Ellin Glasgow]], also aged 40 and a weaver. The return records County Antrim as their birthplace and reports their marriage in '''1831'''; it does not expressly call this a first marriage.<ref name="Census1851">1851 Census of Ireland, Cloughgaldenagh/Galdernaugh house 1, Dunaghy, County Antrim, William Glasgow household, DGS007246617, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L94X-YNNH resident schedule, image 542] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-994X-YNG2 continuation, image 543]; original pages visually inspected in the project source review, 30 October 2026. Retained comparisons: “1851 Irish Census Returns,” detailed public transcription, [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf PDF]; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Killcondray/Dunaghy/Galdernaugh/1/ National Archives of Ireland household page]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QV9Y-WFJ7 FamilySearch record index QV9Y-WFJ7]. These describe the same return, not independent household witnesses.</ref>

The continuation enters “None” for absent household members and for deceased household members. It supplies no additional named relative.<ref name="Census1851"/>

== Research Notes ==
=== Original census review, 30 October 2026 ===

The two original pages confirm the recorded household but do not name William's father or connect him with Robert of Glenleslie. The existing '''36% possible''' father assessment is unchanged. The earlier transcription-based description of 1831 as the couple's ''first'' marriage is superseded: the original reports the year without that restriction. County Antrim is the supported birthplace; crossed-out Dunaghy wording does not establish a certain finer birthplace. “None” in the absent/deceased tables does not establish that William had no other relatives or that every earlier child survived. No date or family attachment is changed.

This completes the original-page inspection previously outstanding. The older source-assessment wording below describes the 22 October review, before that inspection; it does not mean the original remains unread.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1367]] is assessed at 36% (possible). William’s Dunaghy origin, c 1810 birth and established local family fit Robert of Glenleslie, born c 1779 and married in 1803. The selected father is a specific compatible nearby family head, but neither William’s 1851 household nor the older Robert’s household names this relationship.

Possible 36%; local family hypothesis, without a named-son or holding-succession bridge.

Next useful test: Compare William’s marriage and children’s sponsors with the Glenleslie household.

Source basis at the 22 October review: [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf “1851 Irish Census Returns,” Cloughgaldenagh house 1, Dunaghy, County Antrim, detailed public transcription, PDF; see also National Archives of Ireland household page and FamilySearch QV9Y-WFJ7]. No original was newly inspected in that earlier review; no new father was attached. The subsequent original inspection is cited above.


The census does not name William's father. His attachment to [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]] is therefore retained as uncertain and should not be treated as proved by the 1851 household.

The later Griffith's Valuation index for Dunaghy does not list William at Cloughgaldenagh.<ref>“Griffith's Valuation, North Mid Antrim,” Dunaghy index, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1860griffiths/northmidantrimgriffiths.pdf PDF].</ref> This negative finding does not establish his death, migration, or loss of tenancy.
* Death index entry: William Glasgow, 14 September 1874, aged 58, Belfast district, D/1874/49/1007/17/123. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].

== Research Notes ==
=== Late William Alexander Glasgow, named in 1875 ===

Emma’s marriage notice names her father as the late William Alexander Glasgow. She married William, second son of Robert Treacy, on 4 September 1875 at St Thomas’s Church, Belfast. Both spouses were of Parsonstown; that wording does not state her late father’s own residence, birthplace or place of death. His age, occupation, wife and parents are unstated.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1265675182/ Belfast Evening Telegraph, 4 September 1875, p.2].</ref>

An ordinary William with no recorded middle name remains compatible. The Belfast death in 1874 and a possible later daughter fit this family comparison; the 1851 household’s absence of Emma does not exclude a child born later. The source does not identify this William as William Alexander. [[Glasgow-1737|William Glasgow of Killycurragh]], [[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow who died in Ohio in 1855]], and [[Glasgow-3952|William Glasgow associated with County Limerick]] remain lower comparisons. The c.1815 [[Glasgow-2771|Emma Glasgow]] hypothesis cannot be combined with this William’s c.1810 birth.
